title: BiVCoder: A Multi-Agent Framework for Code Generation via Bidirectional Code-Test Diagnosis

problem.claim: Automated code-generation systems need to debug and refine generated code using tests.

gap.claim: Existing test-driven code-generation and refinement frameworks often treat self-generated tests as ground truth, so erroneous tests can lead to ineffective debugging loops and inappropriate code modifications.

contributions.claim: BiVCoder is a diagnosis-driven multi-agent framework with bidirectional code-test diagnosis.
BiVCoder coordinates Coding, Test, and Review Agents, with the Review Agent diagnosing failure root causes and directing repairs to code or tests through an MCP-based execution tool.
BiVCoder-SFT is a role-specific instruction fine-tuning scheme supported by datasets for specializing coding, testing, and reviewing agents.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe the bidirectional code-test diagnosis mechanism as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on HumanEval, MBPP, and their ET variants are reported to show that BiVCoder outperforms the compared approaches.
With GPT-3.5, BiVCoder achieves a reported Pass@1 of 77.3%.
BiVCoder-SFT achieves a reported average score of 79.5% across four datasets, compared with 69.7% for its base model and 77.8% for Qwen3-8B.

narrative_sequence.summary: LLMs have shown potential for automated code generation.
Existing test-driven approaches can fail when self-generated tests are treated as ground truth.
BiVCoder introduces bidirectional diagnosis and coordinates specialized coding, testing, and reviewing agents.
BiVCoder-SFT fine-tunes role-specific agents using constructed datasets.
The authors report improvements across benchmark datasets and for multiple base models.

source_observation.claim: The framework diagnoses whether failures arise from implementation bugs or deficient test cases before triggering targeted repairs.

interpretation.claim: When evaluation artifacts may be unreliable, separating artifact diagnosis from implementation repair may reduce feedback-loop errors.

application.claim: Code-generation workflows could assign explicit roles for coding, test generation, review, execution, and repair routing.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that diagnosis is correct across tasks or that the reported gains generalize beyond the listed benchmarks and models.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the diagnosis procedure, decision criteria, or repair algorithm.
The abstract does not provide experimental baselines, variance, ablations, or evaluation protocols.
The abstract does not describe the constructed datasets or the ET variants in detail.
